Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, LyraShield), Marta Alvarez (Security Eng), Ethan Park (Infra)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE. We want to run through your security posture and hosting constraints. Jordan, Marta — do you want to kick off with your primary concerns?

[00:20] Jordan (CTO): Yeah thanks. We — LyraShield — are evaluating Redwood for a fraud-detection assistant. Two big constraints: one, client PII can't leave our logs or be stored in any third-party datastore without encryption and strong access controls; two, we need evidence for audits — SOC two, ISO27001 — that's kind of non-negotiable for our risk team.

[00:40] Marta (Security Eng): Also we need to confirm SSO integration — SAML or OIDC — SCIM for provisioning. RBAC mapping to our groups is important. And audit logs need to be tamper-evident, with retention for 7 years for certain data classes.

[01:05] Priya (SE): Got it. Quick clarifying q — when you say "PII can't leave our logs" do you mean we can't persist any request/response pairs on the Redwood hosted side, or you're okay with encrypted at-rest storage if the key is yours?

[01:25] Ethan (Infra): Prefer customer-managed keys for anything at rest. Ideally we want a VPC/private deployment with KMS integration or HSM. Hosted could be okay if we can bring our own KMS and guarantee no long-term retention of full transcripts.

[01:45] Alex (AE): Makes sense. High level: Redwood supports Hosted (Redwood-managed), Dedicated (reserved pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For sensitive PII, customers commonly choose Dedicated with customer KMS or full Private. We do have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs — we'll share the artifacts.

[02:10] Jordan: Can you talk specifics: how does RBAC integrate with SSO? Do you support SCIM for group provisioning?

[02:25] Priya: Yes, we support SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning can sync groups to Redwood's RBAC. You can map your IdP groups to roles (admin, ops, reader). There are a couple of nuances — for Dedicated we can set up SAML SSO at the org level, and for Private we can federate to your IdP directly.

[03:00] Marta: Are there audit logs that show who ran what prompts? Can those logs be exported to our SIEM? We need immutable event history for 7 years for some regulated clients.

[03:18] Priya: Audit logs are available per token and per-route. We can stream logs to your logging endpoint (e.g., AWS Kinesis or Splunk). For retention, Hosted logs default to shorter retention but export is supported. In Private deployments, customers control full log retention.

[03:45] Jordan: "Sock two" — sorry — SOC2. We need the actual attestation report and list of controls. Last time we had a vendor we asked for the mapping to our control set. Do you provide control mapping?

[04:00] Alex: Yes, we can provide SOC2 Type II report and a controls matrix mapping to common control frameworks. We'll obfuscate sensitive operational details as required, but you get the evidence required by procurement. I'll attach the PDF after the call.

[04:20] Ethan: Encryption — both in-transit and at-rest. In terms of at-rest, for hosted options can we bring our own key? And if we do, how is it used for caching and KV cache? There's mention in your docs of "KV cache" — is that key-value cache encrypted with the same KMS?

[04:45] Priya: Good question — quick note that some of our generated docs sometimes say KV "cash" in transcripts, sorry for that. For Dedicated we support BYOK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) — keys are used to encrypt persistent storage and snapshots. The KV cache in memory isn't persisted, but prefix/KV caches that are flushed to disk (for warm starts) use the same envelope encryption. For Private/on-prem you can bring an HSM.

[05:20] Marta: If we bring an HSM, who has access to the encryption key? We need separation of duties.

[05:30] Priya: In Private, the key is in your HSM — Redwood doesn't hold the private key. For Dedicated with BYOK, we rotate keys under customer control and provide key usage logs. Access is restricted to service processes; we can share KMS audit logs.

[06:00] Jordan: About retention: you mentioned Hosted default retention is shorter — what are the actual windows? And is there configurable per-customer retention?

[06:15] Alex: Hosted default for request logs is 30 days; transcripts can be configured to auto-delete sooner. For Dedicated we can extend retention per contract — and for Private, you manage retention locally. We'll share the retention matrix.

[06:35] Ethan: On the SSO side, does Redwood support Just-in-Time provisioning? We use SCIM for onboarding and offboarding across all infra.

[06:50] Priya: Yes SCIM is supported. JIT provisioning via SAML assertions is supported for user creation. Group sync is via SCIM. There's a config param in the console to map attributes.

[07:20] Marta: Another item: separation of training/data usage. We can't have any customer data used for model training. Do you support opt-out and attestations for that?

[07:35] Alex: Absolutely — Redwood Hosted offers an explicit data usage opt-out flag on the org. For Dedicated and Private, customer data is never used to update shared models. We'll provide an attestation statement for that as well.

[08:00] Jordan: How about incident response and breach notification SLAs? Our compliance folks want 72-hour disclosure if data is impacted.

[08:15] Priya: Our standard incident response timeline is 72 hours for escalation, and we include customer notifications in SLAs for Dedicated/Private. We'll share the incident response playbook redacted.

[08:40] Ethan: For the pilot we'd want to run a workload simulation: 10 QPS with 1k token payloads, and measure tail latency. Can Redwood run a benchmark in a Dedicated pool and provide logs/audit for the test?

[08:55] Priya: Yes, we can schedule a bench in Dedicated or Private. For Dedicated we'll provision a reserved pool and run the test; logs will be exportable and include request-level tracing. We'll need sample payloads and an agreed time window.

[09:20] Jordan: Cost vs latency tradeoff — we might accept slightly higher p99 if it means we can keep keys in our KMS.

[09:30] Alex: That's a common trade. Private can give you the lowest network surface but may increase ops cost. Dedicated with BYOK often gives the best balance.

[09:55] Marta: One more on audit logs — "tamper-evident" you mentioned. How is that implemented? WORM storage? Signed logs?

[10:10] Priya: We support WORM-mode export to object stores and signed log delivery. For Hosted exports we can push to your S3 bucket with object lock enabled; for Private you control the whole stack.

[10:35] Alex: I'll drop links after the call: SOC2/ISO artifact link (internal), private deployment checklist, KMS integration guide. Note: links will be to redwood-internal pages like https://console.redwood.ai/security/artifacts and a SCIM configuration doc.

[10:55] Jordan: On the procurement side — what legal terms should we expect? Data processing addendum? Standard indemnities?

[11:10] Alex: We have a standard DPA that covers data processing, subprocessor list, and options for EU data residency. For Dedicated and Private we can add more stringent contract language; we'll loop legal if needed.

[11:35] Ethan: Questions on network architecture for Private — do you support air-gapped on-prem deployments?

[11:45] Priya: Yes, we have an on-prem appliance mode for air-gapped environments. It requires a slightly different deployment lifecycle and we provide ops runbooks. We'll include that doc.

[12:05] Marta: For encryption at transit, you support mTLS between the runtime and our services?

[12:15] Priya: Yes, mTLS is supported for inter-service comms in Private and can be configured for Dedicated to backend services.

[12:40] Jordan: Ok practical next steps? I'd like artifacts, and then schedule a pilot in Dedicated with BYOK. We'll need to check budget and timeline internally.

[12:55] Alex: Action items then: I'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test summary; Priya will share the private deployment checklist and KMS integration guide; Jordan will provide data retention policy and sample payloads for benchmarking.

[13:20] Marta: Quick question about log access control — can logs be restricted by role so only auditors can see full transcripts?

[13:35] Priya: Yes RBAC can restrict who can read raw transcripts. We can redact PII at ingestion with policies as well. We'll provide a short example config.

[13:55] Ethan: Any known limitations — e.g., if we use HSM, will that change failover behavior or increase p99?

[14:10] Priya: Using an HSM may add a small token-level latency for key unwrap operations on cold start. We typically mitigate with envelope keys and caching. We'll show benchmark numbers in the pilot.

[14:35] Jordan: Sounds good. Anything else from Redwood?

[14:40] Alex: Just to summarize: we support SAML/SCIM, BYOK/HSM, audit log exports, SOC2/ISO attestations, Private/on-prem option. We'll send artifacts and propose dates for a Dedicated pilot the week of 2026-03-16.

[14:58] Jordan: Perfect. Marta, Ethan — anything else?

[15:05] Marta: No, thanks. Looking forward to the docs.

[15:12] Ethan: Same.

[15:18] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. Priya will follow up with the checklist. We'll log the action items in CRM.

[15:30] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains mild transcription errors (phrasing, acronyms). Shared artifacts referenced: private deployment checklist, SOC2/ISO attestation PDFs, KMS integration guide (links to be provided by Alex).
